notes.meaning: The night was split into watches, which were shifts when guards kept watch. The psalmist wakes before each watch begins so he can think deeply about God's word. He cares more about this than the guards care about their duty. It is better to take time from sleep than to find no time for prayer.

He asks God to listen. He does not lean on his own goodness. He leans on God's loving devotion, God's steady and faithful love. "Give me life" means make me lively and eager to do good. "According to your justice" means according to God's word and promise, because God knows what we need.
His enemies are close at hand and ready to grab him. They chase after evil. They have pushed every thought of God's law far away from them. They are near to all evil but far from God.

The enemies are near to harm him, but God is nearer to save him. When trouble is near, God is near. He is never hard to find. God's commands and promises are true, and no enemy can stop them from coming to pass.

Over a long life he has learned that God's word stands firm. God built it on foundations that last forever. Everyone who has trusted God has found him faithful. The psalmist's faith rests on God's word, which tells him God will help his children when they suffer.

He asks God to look closely at his trouble and rescue him. God wants us to lay our troubles before him and trust him to act in his own time. Remembering God's law does not earn God's help. It shows the heart of a child who trusts a father, and it gives him promises to hold up in prayer.

He asks God to be his lawyer and take up his case against false charges. "Redeem" means to rescue or buy back. Christ is the one who speaks for his people and rescues them. Without God's promise there would be no hope. So he asks God to revive him, or give him new life and strength, as the word promises.

Wicked people do not even look for God's ways. They do not care to learn them. So salvation, God's rescue, is far from them. They may tell themselves they are going to heaven, but the longer they stay in sin, the farther it gets.

God's mercies are tender, many and great. They are like a spring that never runs dry, and they reach every kind of human need. The psalmist asks God to revive him in the way God has promised and in the way God usually treats those who love him.

Many people are against him, yet he does not leave God's word. As long as he holds to it, God is for him, so it does not matter who is against him. A person who stays steady in doing right may have many enemies but need fear none of them.

"The faithless" are like traitors who turn against a good king. Seeing them fills him with deep grief and disgust. He is upset because they dishonor God, not because they bother him. True hatred of sin hates it because it breaks God's word.

He does not say "See how well I keep your commands," because he knows he falls short. He says "See how I love them." Obeying God pleases him only when it comes from love. Loving God's law is a sure sign that we belong to God's family. Still, he asks for life because of God's loving devotion, not because he has earned it.
Take all of God's word together, and the total is truth. Every word, from the first page of Genesis to the end, is true. God has always kept his word, and his fair rulings will stand forever.

Powerful leaders hunt him down without any reason. But he is not afraid of them. He stands in awe of God's word instead. This is deep respect, not the fear of a slave. A heart that fears God more than people is ready to face persecution.

His joy in God's word is like a soldier's joy at finding treasure after a battle is won. Each new thing God shows him in the word feels like a prize. The more we honor God's word, the more joy we find in it.

Love and hate steer the heart. He hates lies, and that includes pretending, false teaching and broken promises. He loves God's law because it is true. We should hate telling a lie even more than being told one, because lying insults God.

"Seven times" means very often, again and again through the day. Even in his troubles he finds reasons to praise God. We can praise God for his fair ways, and even for hard times when God uses them for our good.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The Catholic Church has set times of prayer spread through the day, in a pattern much like this verse describes.

notes.meaning: People who love God's law have deep peace inside, even when there is trouble outside. Nothing becomes a trap that trips them up and makes them fall. People who love the world are let down, but people who love God's word find it gives more than they hoped. They trust God to put all wrongs right in the end.

He hopes for God's salvation, both rescue now and life forever. He also does what God commands. Hope and obedience belong together, and real hope makes us more eager to obey. Faith comes first, and then our works can please God.

He keeps God's word with his whole heart, not just outwardly, and he loves it more than anything. He obeys because he knows God sees every step he takes. Knowing God is always watching should make us careful to obey. People who obey out of love are happy to have their lives looked over by God.

He pictures his cry and his plea traveling up to God's throne. A cry shows how urgent he is, and a plea shows how humble he is. He asks first for understanding and then for rescue, because knowing God's truth comes first. He asks only for what God has promised, trusting God to keep his word.

Praise pours out of him like water from an overflowing spring. He praises God for teaching him. When God opens our minds and hearts, it is so our mouths can praise him. We have learned nothing worthwhile if we have not learned to praise God.

He will sing and speak about God's word, because all of God's commands are right. He wants others to know and follow them too. God's word should guide all we say, so we neither speak wrongly nor keep silent when we should speak.

He knows his own strength is not enough, and no person can truly help him. So he asks God to stretch out his strong hand. He has chosen God's ways on purpose, over every other thing, and those who choose God's ways can count on God's help.

He longs for God's salvation. That means rescue from an evil world and, in the end, eternal life with God. Meanwhile God's law is his greatest delight. Those who look forward to God's salvation should take joy in his ways now.

He wants to keep living so he can praise God. "Your judgments" are God's word and God's care over him, which are his only reason to hope for help. He asks God to use all of these to strengthen him for a life of praise.

The psalm ends with honest confession. He has wandered like a lost sheep that cannot find its own way back. So he asks God, the good Shepherd, to come and find him. Even believers wander, but they still remember God's commands and know who to look to. When God seeks, he always finds.
